note: Two amqp-value sections: the artifact's body is one of three choices, and the third choice is a single amqp-value section. A decoder that read them as a sequence would hand its caller a message whose body the artifact does not define. Reading: amqp:decode-error, since the structure is stated by the occurrence list and no condition is named for a violation of it.
A data section followed by an amqp-sequence section: the body is one of the three choices, not a mixture of two of them. Reading: amqp:decode-error.

Two header sections, where the structure list gives at most one. This matters because a second header is not merely redundant: which one a consumer honoured would decide durability and priority. Reading: amqp:decode-error.
A header, a footer, and then a data section: the footer is the tail of the annotated message, so a section after it has no place in the structure. Reading: amqp:decode-error.

A data section followed by a properties section: properties is part of the bare message's head, and the body follows it. This is the pure order case, with both sections individually well formed, so a decoder that dispatched on section type alone would accept it. Reading: amqp:decode-error.

A complete empty header, then two octets that begin a second section and stop: 005370c0 is the descriptor and a list8 constructor with no size. The first section decodes and the read of the second fails, which is where a loop over sections must fail rather than return the prefix it managed. Reason class: truncated.

A data section followed by a described value whose descriptor no declared type carries (00 53 ff, ulong 255). The message has a valid body and then an octet sequence that is not a section, so the refusal has to come from the section read rather than from the structure rule. Reading: amqp:decode-error.

A payload carrying one header section and nothing else. The reading pinned here is that the structure list is a sequence — zero or one of each head section, the body as one of its three choices, zero or one footer — so a payload that carries a section and no body is not a message; the other reading would admit this as a message with one section, and the zero-octet payload is the exemption rather than an instance of the same case, because a transfer with no payload carries no message at all. The two sides of the rule are here and in msg-bare-properties-data (a body-bearing message admitted) and msg-empty (the exemption admitted), so disabling the rule makes this vector stop failing rather than making every message vector fail. Octets: 00 53 70 c0 02 01 41 — the header descriptor, a two-octet list8 holding one boolean.
